abstract: ackground and aims: Effective therapeutic interventions for Drug induced liver injury (DILI) remain limited. N-myc downstream regulated gene-1 (NDRG1), a stress-responsive proteins, has an incompletely defined role in acetaminophen-induced liver injury. Method: Wild-type (WT), NDRG1Hep-flox, Hepatocyte-specific NDRG1 conditional knockout mice (NDRG1Hep-KO) were subjected to APAP-induced injury modeling. Liver and blood sample from patient were analyzed. Liver sample of mice subsequently underwent RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq), untargeted metabolomic profiling, single-cell sequencing, succinylation sequencing. For in vitro studies, AML-12 hepatocytes, RAW264.7 macrophages, and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs), human Monocyte-Derived Macrophages, human hepatocyte organoids were utilized in experiments. Result: NDRG1 was upregulated in mouse and human DILI livers. NDRG1 conditional knockout significantly exacerbates DILI. Mechanistically, NDRG1 inhibited GAMT ubiquitination to enhance creatine production, and hepatocyte?derived creatine attenuated M1 polarization of liver macrophages by suppressing PHB1 succinylation at lysine 128. CXCL2? macrophages were identified as a major subpopulation regulated by NDRG1. Conclusion: Hepatocyte NDRG1 protects against APAP-DILI by driving GAMT-dependent creatine production and PHB1 K128 succinylation-dependent macrophage reprogramming.
